title: Global publics are retreating toward local trust, personal control and present-focused coping as technology, institutions and climate feel less governable
geography: 38-market cross-national survey; market-average comparisons and global thematic synthesis

denominator.unit: adults interviewed by Ipsos Global Advisor across 38 markets; global score is an unadjusted average across markets, not population-weighted

government_not_prioritising_concerns.unit: percent saying their government does not prioritise their concerns

economy_rigged.unit: percent believing the economy is rigged in favour of the rich and powerful

country_should_be_like_it_was.unit: percent wanting their country to be like it was

future_past_counterpoint.unit: percent saying they would want to have grown up when their parents were children

observations.method: Ipsos Global Advisor online survey with country-level weighting to demographic profiles; 38-market thematic synthesis.
observations.uncertainty: Online samples in some markets are more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population; market-average results should not be read as a population-weighted global estimate or causal explanation.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 18+ in India, 18–74 in specified markets, 16–74 in other markets; approximately 1,000 respondents in 20 markets and 500 in 18 markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Nostalgia and economic-rigging judgments may reflect current political framing or generalized dissatisfaction rather than a literal desire to restore past institutions or policies.

observations.period: 2026; trust, identity and consumer coping themes

denominator.unit: Ipsos Global Trends survey respondents across 38 markets

personal_autonomy.unit: percent agreeing it is up to everyone to work out their own principles to guide decisions

local_values_trust.value: Trust is becoming more personal, local and values-driven, with familiar brands, relatable individuals and local organisations gaining importance

identity_through_purchases.value: Consumers increasingly use purchases to shape identity and pursue personal progress

observations.method: Cross-market attitudinal trend analysis combining repeated Global Trends measures with 2026 thematic interpretation.
observations.uncertainty: The public thematic pages do not establish whether local or values-based trust translates into durable purchasing, political participation or institutional repair.
observations.subgroup: Adults across the 38 markets, with country-level variation in the underlying survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Personalisation and local trust may be compensatory responses to institutional failure, but they can also fragment common standards and make accountability more difficult.

denominator.unit: Ipsos Global Trends survey respondents across 38 markets

enjoy_today_orientation.value: A growing majority in many markets agree it is important to enjoy life today and let tomorrow take care of itself

traditional_milestones.value: Home ownership, career progression and family life remain desirable but feel harder to achieve for younger generations

government_help_concern.unit: percent worrying their government will do too little to help people in the years ahead

hard_work_fairness.value: Sentiment that hard work is rewarded fairly is declining in many countries

observations.method: Cross-market trend interpretation connecting aspirations, institutional expectations and consumer coping.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not quantify the full country distribution or isolate affordability, housing, labor-market, family-policy and institutional causes of changed time horizons.
observations.subgroup: Adults across 38 markets, with life-stage and country variation in the underlying measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Present-focused consumption may be resilience and pleasure-seeking under uncertainty rather than nihilism or withdrawal from long-term planning.

denominator.unit: Ipsos Global Trends survey respondents across 38 markets; year-on-year comparisons use the relevant repeated measures

technology_concern_direction.value: Concern is increasing as the pace of technological change intensifies

ai_positivity_decline.value: Positivity toward AI declined between 2025 and 2026 in several AI-leading markets including Singapore, South Korea, Hong Kong SAR and Great Britain

control_question.value: People are asking who benefits from technology, who controls it and how it will affect their lives

observations.method: Repeated cross-market technology-attitude comparison and thematic analysis of AI sentiment.
observations.uncertainty: The public thematic page does not provide the underlying country percentages or distinguish AI applications; declining positivity may reflect specific labor, climate, privacy or governance concerns.
observations.subgroup: Adults across the 38 markets, including younger citizens and AI-leading markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rising concern can represent a demand for governance and usable safeguards rather than rejection of technological adoption.

denominator.unit: Ipsos Global Trends survey respondents across 38 markets

personal_climate_action_saturation.unit: percent saying they are doing all they can personally to fight climate change

climate_concern.value: Climate concern remains high but has plateaued

adaptation_expectation.value: People increasingly expect organisations to help them adapt to climate change in practical ways

holistic_health.value: Physical and mental health are increasingly treated as equally important, with food, medicine, exercise and environment folded into wellness

observations.method: Cross-market climate and health-attitude analysis within the Global Trends program.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not show the country distribution behind the 70% climate figure or specify which organisational adaptation actions people prioritise; holistic wellness language may include both prevention and commercial optimisation.
observations.subgroup: Adults across 38 markets, with market-specific differences in climate exposure, health systems and consumer access.
observations.counterinterpretation: Climate-concern plateauing may signal normalization and adaptation under chronic exposure, not reduced climate risk or indifference.

boundary: This record adds a cross-market cultural mechanism: when institutions, technology and the future feel less controllable, publics combine nostalgia, personal autonomy, local/value-based trust and present-focused consumption, while demanding practical adaptation from organisations. It is a weighted online-attitude survey and thematic interpretation, not a population-weighted world estimate, causal model, behavioral transaction dataset or forecast.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Ipsos Global Trends archive, methodology page and thematic pages for trust, nostalgia, social fracture, consumer coping, technology, health and climate were retrieved and reviewed; the archive HTML was hashed.
